title: Universal frame models, frame pullback and geometric goodness
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $A$ an $\mathcal O_S$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use tensor inverse images and their canonical composition comparison [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $h:X\to Z$, let $c_h:h^*\mathcal O_Z\simeq\mathcal O_X$ be the canonical structure-sheaf comparison, the tensor-pullback comparison with ordinary pullback [def-sc-tensor-pullback-power-comparison] followed by the unit comparison of ordinary pullback. For $f:X\to S$, a frame $e:\mathcal O_X\simeq f^*A$, and $h:U\to X$, define $\operatorname{pullFrame}(A,f,e,h)$ to be $\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{c_h^{-1}}h^*\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{h^*e}h^*f^*A\xrightarrow{\sim}(f\circ h)^*A$, using the inverse of the normalized composition comparison. A frame model of $A$ consists of an $S$-scheme $p:F\to S$ and a universal frame $e_F:\mathcal O_F\simeq p^*A$ such that for every $S$-scheme $f:U\to S$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}_S(U,F)\to\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U,f^*A)$, sending $a$ to the pullback of $e_F$ along $a$ and identifying $p\circ a=f$, is bijective. Write $F.\operatorname{at}(a)$ for this evaluated frame. This defines data of a representing model, without asserting its existence for arbitrary $A$. For a field $k$ [def-weil-field], a scheme $X$ and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, write $\operatorname{Good}(X,f)$ for the conjunction that $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], its diagonal $X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}X$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $f$ is locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].
